About Chamber

Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death in America. At Chamber, we’re rebuilding the system for cardiology, creating a world where outcomes, not volume, define success. We partner with independent cardiologists to help them lead population health efforts in their communities, equipping them with technology, data, and operational tools that turn complex insights into better care for patients.

Our model blends clinical expertise, thoughtful design, and a modern operating platform that supports physicians, patients, and payers alike. We believe innovation and empathy go hand in hand, and by combining cutting-edge AI tools with a relentless focus on human care, we can transform heart health at scale.

Role Overview

The Community Health Worker (CHW) will play a key role in connecting patients to Chamber’s cardiology care programs through non-clinical outreach and engagement. This is a hands-on, patient-facing role for someone who builds trust easily, enjoys helping people navigate the healthcare system, and is excited to make a difference in the cardiovascular health of the communities we serve.

The role will work closely with care coordinators, clinicians, and operations teams to support value-based care programs, document patient interactions accurately, and share insights from the field that help shape how Chamber engages patients.

Key Responsibilities

  • Conducting outbound phone calls to assigned patient populations on behalf of the applicable Payor program, while meeting expectations for call volume and call quality.

  • Communicating the purpose of outreach and its connection to the patient's health plan support services.

  • Address social determinants of health (SDOH) by connecting patients to food, housing, transportation, and other resources, and closing the referral loop to confirm needs were met

  • Develop and implement patient-centered care plans based on patient-stated goals and transition-of-care (TOC) needs

  • Coordinate care with external providers, including scheduling and confirming appointment attendance

  • Coordinate health insurance benefits and related support, such as recertification paperwork, incentives, food assistance, and utility support

  • Collaborate with the interdisciplinary care team, and escalate internally or to a higher level of clinical support as needed, seeing escalations through to resolution

  • Accessing applicable EHR systems and care management platforms — which may span multiple Payor and practice environments — to retrieve discharge notifications, ADT feeds, and relevant patient records

  • Maintain working knowledge of local community resources to make appropriate connections and close the loop

  • Handle administrative tasks such as faxing to provider practices and uploading to internal systems

  • Recording patient responses accurately and completely, without interpretation or modification

  • Provide patient coaching and education on healthy habits, disease prevention, self-management, and nutrition

  • Serve as patient advocate and trusted bridge between the patient, health system, and community

  • Identify and address barriers to care

  • Identify and escalate clinical, safety, or social concerns per established Chamber protocol

Requirements

  • High school diploma, or GED

  • 3+ years of Community Health Worker experience

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to deliver direct, constructive feedback.

  • HIPAA knowledge and comfort handling protected health information.

  • Must be comfortable operating in ambiguity, adapting quickly as programs evolve, and building in motion.

  • Upkeep of electronic calendars and scheduling systems (e.g., Microsoft Outlook) to coordinate meetings, appointments, and time off

  • Documenting all patient encounters and health data in EHRs and/or Care Management platforms, ensuring timely and accurate entry

  • Ability to operate Chamber’s communication platform(s), included but not limited to: Slack, Microsoft teams

  • Troubleshooting basic connectivity, device, or platform issues, and escalating to manager or IT support when needed

  • Access to a dedicated, private workspace that supports HIPAA-compliant phone communication and compliance standards.

  • Basic understanding of medical terminology, human anatomy and common conditions and treatments

Preferred:

  • Bilingual (English/Spanish)

Location

  • Remote opportunity, must be based in the United States.

  • Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
